reasons: No migrations, so table changes do not reach existing databases.

terms.meaning: A Python library for talking to databases using Python classes.
The object that holds the connection to the database.
A short working space for reading and writing database rows.
A small database stored in a single file.
A link from one table row to a row in another table that must exist.
A managed change to a database structure over time.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Connection setup
sections.what: Creates the database engine, turns on foreign key checks for SQLite, and builds the session factory and base class for tables.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared connection setup for the whole backend.
sections.watch_out: The foreign key switch only applies to SQLite databases.

sections.name: get_db
sections.title: Per-request session
sections.what: Opens a database session for a web request and closes it when the request ends.
sections.why: Likely reason: prevents sessions from being left open.
sections.watch_out: The return type says Session, but the function yields one, which is a looser contract than it looks.

sections.name: get_db_context
sections.title: Session for scripts
sections.what: Provides the same open-and-close behaviour for scripts or one-off tasks.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets non-web code use the database safely.
sections.watch_out: Code that forgets to use the with statement can leave sessions open.

sections.name: init_db
sections.title: Create tables
sections.what: Imports the models and creates every table that does not exist yet.
sections.why: Likely reason: sets up a new database in one call.
sections.watch_out: Existing tables are not updated when the models change.

sections.name: drop_all
sections.title: Drop all tables
sections.what: Deletes every table and all their data.
sections.why: Likely reason: for resetting a development database.
sections.watch_out: This erases all data with no confirmation. Never run it against real data.

summary: Sets up the database connection, gives code a way to open a session, and creates or drops all tables.
purpose: The connection layer that every database operation uses.
why: Likely reason: one shared setup for the whole backend. SQLite foreign key checks are switched on because SQLite leaves them off by default.
how: Creates the engine from the database address. For SQLite, allows multi-thread use and turns on foreign keys for each connection. Builds a session factory and a base class for tables. get_db gives FastAPI a session per request and closes it afterwards. get_db_context does the same for scripts. init_db creates tables from the models. drop_all deletes them.
inputs: The database_url setting and the table definitions in models.py.
outputs: Database sessions and tables in the database.
risks: drop_all deletes all data with no confirmation. init_db creates only missing tables and does not change existing ones, and no migration tool is visible. The declarative base import location is older and may warn with newer SQLAlchemy.
debug: For no such table errors, run init_db. For foreign key errors, confirm the database is SQLite. For connection failures, check database_url in the .env file.
